title: Foundry and Azure AI Evaluation evaluators
summary: Foundry ships built-in evaluators for quality, RAG, safety and agents, plus custom evaluators, through two SDK paths. Many are preview. Choose by what you can label, which tools your agent calls and whether a preview dependency is acceptable.
useIf: You build on Foundry or Azure and want portal-visible scores, safety evaluators and CI-friendly runs.
avoidIf: You need a feature with an SLA today and the evaluator you want is preview, or your agent uses tools the evaluators barely support.

explain.md: The built-in catalog has families: general purpose (Coherence, Fluency), textual similarity (Similarity, F1, BLEU, GLEU, ROUGE, METEOR), RAG, risk and safety, agent, rubric (preview), Azure OpenAI graders and custom (preview). Microsoft suggests RAG = Retrieval + Groundedness + Relevance + Content Safety, and agents = Output Quality + Tool Use Quality + Rubric + Content Safety [[r2]].

items: **Composite evaluators.** `builtin.output_quality` batches Fluency, Coherence, Intent Resolution, Task Adherence, Groundedness and Task Completion into one judge call. `builtin.tool_use_quality` batches five tool metrics. Default pass thresholds are 3 on 1 to 5 scales and 1 on 0/1 scales, and the primary result passes only if every applicable component passes [[r3]].
**Levels.** `evaluation_level` is `turn` (default) or `conversation`. Conversation level needs the `messages` format and skips turn-only evaluators [[r2]].

**Custom evaluators (preview).** Code-based returns a float from Python `grade(sample, item)`. Prompt-based returns JSON with `result` and `reason`. Endpoint-based returns `score`, `reason`, `status` and optional `properties` [[r41]]. Foundry also recommends a **rubric evaluator** (preview) as the primary agent measure: weighted dimensions applied by an LLM judge, hand-written or generated from the agent's name, instructions and tools [[tr5]].

**Two SDK paths.** Classic `azure-ai-evaluation` (1.18.8 released 2026-10-09) with `evaluate()`, and new cloud evaluation through `azure-ai-projects` (2.2.0 or later, latest 2.8.0 on 2026-10-05) using `AIProjectClient` and `get_openai_client()`. The classic agent article does not apply to the new portal, so check each page's banner [[r38]].

explain.title: Tool coverage and a deprecated grader
explain.md: Agent evaluators fully support File Search, Function tool, MCP and Knowledge-based MCP. For Azure AI Search, Bing Grounding, Bing Custom Search, SharePoint Grounding, Code Interpreter, Fabric Data Agent and Web Search, avoid `tool_call_accuracy`, `tool_input_accuracy`, `tool_output_utilization`, `tool_call_success` and `groundedness`. Quality Grader is deprecated even though one catalog page still lists it as preview [[r3]].

pitfalls.symptom: Tool Call Accuracy returns odd scores for an agent that uses Azure AI Search
pitfalls.cause: That tool has limited evaluator support
pitfalls.fix: Avoid the four tool metrics and groundedness there, grade the outcome or write a custom evaluator

pitfalls.symptom: Code samples fail against the new portal
pitfalls.cause: A classic SDK article was followed (`azure-ai-evaluation`) for a new-portal project
pitfalls.fix: Read the banner, and use `azure-ai-projects` 2.x for new cloud evaluation

pitfalls.symptom: A build breaks after an evaluator was renamed or withdrawn
pitfalls.cause: Preview feature, or Quality Grader which is deprecated
pitfalls.fix: Pin versions, keep a fallback code check and watch the docs for status changes

scenarios.title: Agent that calls Azure AI Search and Bing
scenarios.situation: A Foundry agent answers questions using Azure AI Search and Bing Grounding. The team wants a tool-quality score in the dashboard and a CI gate.
unknowns: Can the outcome be checked in code?
Is a rubric evaluator acceptable as preview?
scenarios.question: How do you score tool use?

options.name: Outcome check plus rubric or custom evaluator, with tool metrics skipped for those tools
options.why: The docs say to avoid the four tool metrics and groundedness for these tools, so grade what the agent achieved and encode your own rules.
options.tradeoff: More effort than built-ins, and rubric and custom evaluators are preview.

options.name: Use `builtin.tool_use_quality` anyway
options.why: The composite includes metrics that are documented as unsupported for these tools, so scores mislead.
options.tradeoff: Right for agents that use Function tool, MCP or File Search.

options.name: Skip tool evaluation and rely on thumbs up and down
options.tradeoff: No gate and no step-level signal.

flips.if: The agent switches to function tools or MCP

flips.then: Write code-based checks and keep them local.

scenarios.takeaway: Check tool coverage before you trust a tool metric.

scenarios.title: Fast CI on an Agent Framework app
scenarios.situation: A team builds with Agent Framework in Python and merges 20 times a day. Cloud judge runs take minutes and cost tokens. They still want safety coverage before release.
scenarios.question: How do you split local and cloud evaluators?

options.name: `LocalEvaluator` code checks per PR, Foundry evaluators nightly and before release
options.why: Deterministic checks (`keyword_check`, `tool_called_check`) give fast feedback and cloud judges and safety evaluators run where cost and time are acceptable.

options.name: Cloud evaluators on every PR
options.why: It slows merges and burns judge spend.
options.tradeoff: Fine with a handful of merges a week.

options.name: Safety evaluators only at launch
options.tradeoff: Safety regressions between launches go unseen.

flips.if: Merges drop to a few a week
flips.then: Run cloud evaluators on each PR.

flips.if: A policy needs semantic judgement per change
flips.then: Add a small prompt-based custom evaluator to the PR suite.

scenarios.takeaway: Local checks for speed, cloud judges for depth.

quiz.q: A composite evaluator such as `builtin.tool_use_quality` reports its primary result as pass when...
options: The average component score is above the threshold
quiz.explain: The primary result passes only if every applicable component passes. Averaging or any-pass would hide a failing component.

flashcards.front: Which two SDK paths exist for Foundry evaluation?
flashcards.back: Classic `azure-ai-evaluation` with `evaluate()`, and new cloud evaluation via `azure-ai-projects` 2.x with `AIProjectClient` and `get_openai_client()`. Docs mix both, so read the banner.

flashcards.front: Default pass thresholds for composite agent evaluators?
flashcards.back: 3 on 1 to 5 scales and 1 on 0/1 scales. The primary result passes only if every applicable component passes.

flashcards.back: Azure AI Search, Bing Grounding, Bing Custom Search, SharePoint Grounding, Code Interpreter, Fabric Data Agent and Web Search. Avoid four tool metrics and groundedness there.
